name: Accounts Statistics for the Non-Agricultural Private Sector (Regnskabsstatistik for private byerhverv), firm accounts survey
owner: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik)
description: Annual mandatory survey of a sample of firms in the non-agricultural private sector (all large firms plus a size-stratified sample of smaller ones, roughly 8,000-9,000 firms around 1999-2003) reporting detailed income statement, balance sheet, investment and employment/hours items; combined with tax-register data for non-sampled firms.

documents.title: Regnskabsstatistik 2025 - kladde (draft of the full online reporting form: all questions)

access: Firm-level microdata (FIRE/REGN registers) via Statistics Denmark researcher access (forskeradgang), linkable to IDA/employer-employee data.
notes: Only the current (2025) reporting form is online; no questionnaire for the 1999-2003 waves used by Bagger et al. (2014) was found. The 2025 draft's question text is embedded as vector graphics (not extractable text) but was confirmed visually (e.g. p.3: Resultatopgørelse items 1-6). Reporter page with XBRL template: https://www.dst.dk/da/Indberet/oplysningssider/regnskabsstatistik. Bagger et al. describe the data in Section 4 and Appendix B (sampling scheme) of the UCL working-paper version.

name: Children and Youth in Denmark (CYD) / Børn og unge i Danmark - velfærd og trivsel
owner: SFI - Danish National Centre for Social Research, now VIVE (funded by Bikubenfonden)
description: Repeated cross-section of random samples of Danish children aged about 3, 7, 11, 15 and 19 (2009 and 2013; later rounds 2017/2018); parents of the 3- and 7-year-olds and the older children themselves answer by web with telephone follow-up (11-year-olds by personal interview), linked to Statistics Denmark registers.

documents.title: Børn og unge i Danmark - velfærd og trivsel 2010 (SFI report on the 2009 survey)
documents.location: Appendix Bilag 1, pp. 248-253: list of indicators by domain and age group (indicator descriptions, not full question wording)

documents.title: Børn og unge i Danmark - velfærd og trivsel 2014 (SFI report on the 2013 survey)
documents.location: Introduction 'Undersøgelsens datagrund og metoder' (pp. ~21-27) describes the questionnaire design and modes; Bilag 1 (methods)

access: Survey microdata are held by VIVE; researchers gain access through a VIVE agreement and analyse them linked to registers on Statistics Denmark's research servers.
notes: Rossin-Slater and Wüst use the 2009 CYD wave (custody arrangements), pooled with DALSC 2007 (Appendix C). No questionnaire PDF or codebook found online for 2009 or 2013. The paper's source link (sfi.dk/children_and_young_people_in_denmark-7395.aspx) is defunct and the Wayback Machine could not be reached. No Danish Data Archive study page found.
waves_used: as used by Rossin-Slater and Wüst (2018)

name: Copenhagen Life Panel (CLP)
owner: Copenhagen Life Panel research team, Department of Economics / CEBI, University of Copenhagen
description: Online panel survey of a random sample of adults drawn from the Danish population register, fielded every January since 2020 and linkable to Statistics Denmark administrative registers; the January 2021 wave carried the conditional earnings-expectations instrument of Caplin et al.

documents.title: Online Appendix for 'Subjective Earnings Risk' (Caplin, Gregory, Lee, Leth-Petersen, Sæverud), Appendix A: Survey questions (CLP January 2021 earnings-expectations module, with variable names and routing)

notes: No public CLP project website, full-panel questionnaire or codebook was found; only the earnings-risk module (in the St. Louis Fed WP 2023-003 online appendix, dated April 2025) is documented. The ReStud online appendix itself was not located; the restud.com paper page links no supplementary files.

description: Monthly repeated cross-section of about 1,500 residents aged 16-74 drawn from the CPR register, interviewed by telephone/web as the first module of Statistics Denmark's Omnibus survey; questions are harmonised with the European Commission's consumer survey and include quantitative inflation perceptions and expectations.

name: Danish Expenditure Survey / Household Budget Survey (Forbrugsundersøgelsen)
owner: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik)
description: Annual (since 1994) sample survey of private households combining a face-to-face/CAPI interview on fixed and large expenditures over the past 12 months with a 14-day expenditure diary (regnskabshæfte), supplemented with register data; results are usually published as pooled three-year samples.

documents.title: Forbrugsundersøgelsen - Metodebeskrivelse: Fra dataindsamling til offentliggørelse (Danmarks Statistik 1999; describes the post-1994 design, interview topics, diaries, coding and weighting; Bilag lists fieldwork materials)
Statistikdokumentation: Forbrugsundersøgelsen (current documentation; yearly PDFs for 2013-2024)

access: Microdata via Statistics Denmark's Research Service (register-linkable household files); no public-use file.
notes: No interview questionnaire (interviewskema) or expenditure diary for 1994-1996, or for any later year, was found online at dst.dk, nor a DDA/Rigsarkivet study page; the 1999 method description describes the interview content but does not reproduce question wording. The papers using it do not reproduce questions.

name: Danish Health and Morbidity Survey 2000 / Danish National Health Interview Survey (Sundheds- og sygelighedsundersøgelsen 2000, SUSY 2000)
owner: National Institute of Public Health (Statens Institut for Folkesundhed, SIF; now part of University of Southern Denmark)
description: Nationally representative health survey of adults in Denmark combining a personal (face-to-face) interview by Statistics Denmark field staff and a self-administered questionnaire; run in 1987, 1994, 2000, 2005, then as self-administered surveys 2010 onward. The 2000 wave had about 22,500 sampled persons (national, follow-up and county supplementary samples).

notes: Health insurance (supplerende sundhedsforsikring) questions appear in the personal interview (around pp. 71-72 of both interview versions). Older 1987/1994 and later 2005+ questionnaires are also on the landing page.

owner: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik)
description: Quarterly rotating-panel sample survey of persons aged 15-89 (earlier 15-74) resident in Denmark, the Danish part of the EU-LFS; interviews by telephone (CATI) and, since 2016, also web (CAWI), about labour market status in a fixed reference week.

name: Danish Time Use Survey 2001 (DTUS; Danish: Tidsanvendelsesundersøgelsen 2001 / Danskernes tidsanvendelse 2001)
owner: SFI - Danish National Institute of Social Research (now VIVE), with Rockwool Foundation Research Unit; fieldwork by SFI-Survey
description: Nationally representative survey of 2,739 Danes aged 16-74 (2001; split sample spring/autumn): CAPI home interview with a questionnaire on background, normal weekly paid and household work hours, personal expenditures and well-being, plus self-completed 10-minute time diaries for one weekday and one weekend day by respondent and partner (6,624 diaries); linked to Statistics Denmark registers. Repeat of the 1987 survey; followed by the 2008/09 Danish Time Use and Consumption Survey.

documents.title: Browning & Gørtz (2006), Spending Time and Money within the Household, Oxford Economics Discussion Paper 288 (the data description Foerster cites, fn. 18): quotes the DTUS 2001 personal-expenditure questions and describes the normal-hours housework/market-work questions

documents.location: Tables 1-2 and text, PDF pp. 6-8

documents.title: Bonke (2002), Tid og velfærd, SFI rapport 02:26 - main report; Kapitel 6 'Data og bortfald' lists questionnaire and diary contents, sampling and non-response

access: Microdata held by VIVE (formerly SFI) / Rockwool Foundation; researchers access linked survey-register data via a Statistics Denmark research project (no public download found; not located in the DDA catalogue).
notes: The original DTUS 2001 CAPI questionnaire and diary form were not found online (searched VIVE/SFI, Rockwool Foundation, MTUS - which lists Denmark 2001 only as a harmonised simple file with no documentation - and Danish National Archives). Only partial verbatim question wording is available via Browning & Gørtz (2006); Bonke WP 26:2002 describes but does not quote the household-work items. The 1987 questionnaire documentation (MTUS readme) was not checked.

name: Danish Work Environment Cohort Study (DWECS) / Den Nationale Arbejdsmiljøkohorte (NAK)
owner: National Research Centre for the Working Environment (NFA; formerly Arbejdsmiljøinstituttet, AMI)
description: Panel/split-panel survey of a representative sample of the Danish workforce (employees and self-employed, initially aged 18-59), interviewed by Statistics Denmark (phone/personal interview, later questionnaire) about every five years from 1990 to 2010; responses are linkable to registers.
access: Via NFA (contact nfa@nfa.dk) and Statistics Denmark researcher access (forskeradgang) for register-linked versions; project-specific approval.
notes: No questionnaire for the 1995 or 2000 waves found online (searched nfa.dk, arbejdsmiljoforskning.dk, DDA, Eurofound). Taber & Vejlin (2020) Appendix B describes the data but does not reproduce the question on who initiated job termination. The NFA research-data page only lists NAK2005 data on request. Burr et al. (2003, SJWEH 29(4):270-279) describe the 1990-2000 waves.

name: European Community Household Panel (ECHP); Danish part sometimes called Det Europæiske Husstandspanel
owner: Eurostat, fielded in Denmark by the Danish National Institute of Social Research (SFI, now VIVE)
description: Harmonised annual household panel run in the EU member states 1994-2001 (eight waves), with a household questionnaire and a personal questionnaire for every member aged 16+, covering income, employment, job satisfaction, health, housing and social relations; the Danish sample was drawn from the CPR register and can be linked to IDA/registers.

documents.title: Clark, Kristensen and Westergård-Nielsen, 'Job Satisfaction and Co-worker Wages: Status or Signal?', IZA DP 3073 - quotes the ECHP overall job-satisfaction item used ('How satisfied are you with your work or other main activity?', 1-6 scale)
documents.location: Section 3.1 'The Data', p. 10 (single question quoted in text; not a full questionnaire)

documents.title: The EC Household Panel Newsletter (01/02), Eurostat 2003 (sample sizes by wave and country)

access: Anonymised ECHP UDB microdata via Eurostat's microdata access procedure for research entities; the register-linked Danish file is held by VIVE/Statistics Denmark and used on DST research servers.
notes: No ECHP questionnaire (household/personal, generic or Danish) was found online. The Eurostat ECHP library (CIRCABC 'echpanel' Library, PAN documents) now requires EU Login; the EPUNet ECHP user guide site (epunet.essex.ac.uk) no longer resolves and the Wayback Machine is unreachable from this environment. No DDA/Rigsarkivet study page for the Danish ECHP was found.

name: International Social Survey Programme 2002: Family and Changing Gender Roles III (ISSP 2002, GESIS ZA3880; Danish component 'ISSP Family 2002')
owner: ISSP Research Group; archived by GESIS (ZA3880). Danish component run by the Danish ISSP programme (Aalborg University, Jørgen Goul Andersen)
description: Cross-national attitude module on women's employment, family, childcare and division of housework fielded in 34 countries in 2002-03. In Denmark: simple random sample of 2,100 from the CPR register, postal self-completion survey with telephone follow-up, 21 Nov 2002 - 28 Feb 2003, 1,379 respondents (66.2% response). ISSP modules repeat roughly every 10 years (1988, 1994, 2002, 2012).

documents.title: ZA Study 3880 Codebook: ISSP 2002 Family and Changing Gender Roles III (GESIS Zentralarchiv, 2004) - includes per-country study descriptions and full English source question wording for every item

access: Integrated data file (ZA3880, doi:10.4232/1.11564) downloadable free from GESIS after registration; Danish national file also at the Danish National Archives (DDA).
notes: GESIS pages (gesis.org, search.gesis.org) return Cloudflare 403 from this environment, so the official Source Questionnaire (ZA3880_bq.pdf) and the Danish country questionnaire on the GESIS ZA3880 page could not be opened or verified; the landing page URL was taken from search results, not opened. The verified codebook is the official GESIS codebook but is hosted on a third-party (SAGE companion) site. No Danish-language questionnaire found.

name: Incentivised online time-discounting experiment and survey (Epper, Fehr, Fehr-Duda, Kreiner, Lassen, Leth-Petersen and Rasmussen)
owner: Authors (CEBI, University of Copenhagen / University of Zurich)
description: Online experiment run in 2015 with a random sample of middle-aged Danes (3,620 completers) invited by letter. It elicits time, risk and social preferences with real payouts to NemKonto and is linked to administrative wealth registers. A 2015 follow-up with 2,096 respondents and a 2018 study with 4,151 Danes born 1967-1986 also asked the 1973 DLSY preferred-income-profile question.
